sentences.text: The only known species, Vorona berivotrensis, is represented by scattered hindlimb bones that may belong to a single individual.
The fossil remains of Vorona display a mix of features found in both primitive and modern birds.
The genus Vorona is known from fossils found in the Late Cretaceous Maevarano Formation near the village of Berivotra in Madagascar.
Some researchers suggest that Vorona might be a primitive member of the ornithuromorph group.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Vorona as Ornithuromorpha.
The Maevarano Formation where Vorona fossils were found dates to the Campanian stage, between 70.6 and 83.5 million years ago.
Fossil occurrences of Vorona are also recorded from the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
Other studies have classified Vorona as an enantiornithean bird.
Confusion with the dromaeosaurid Rahonavis ostromi led to the incorrect idea that Vorona possessed a sickle-shaped claw on each foot.
